title: MVVM and Other App Architecture Patterns
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of mvvm and other app architecture patterns in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply model-view-viewmodel in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on mvvm and other app architecture patterns and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Model-View-ViewModel”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Application code connects state, UI, APIs, data storage and platform capabilities. Clear ownership and explicit failure states make the experience more reliable and accessible.

content_blocks.title: Reference Lifetime and ARC
content_blocks.alt_text: The diagram shows how two strong references can form a cycle and why a weak reference can break the cycle when the lifetime model permits it.
content_blocks.caption: Strong reference cycles can keep class instances alive.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

**Work through the lesson.** Keep SwiftUI state ownership and data flow predictable while composing reusable screens and architecture. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Model-View-ViewModel
items.text: SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

items.title: Service and repository boundaries
items.text: For service and repository boundaries, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

items.title: Separation of presentation and business logic
items.text: For separation of presentation and business logic, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

items.title: Selecting an architecture appropriate to project size
items.text: ARC manages class-instance lifetimes through references. Strong cycles can keep instances alive; use `weak` or `unowned` only when the ownership/lifetime model justifies it.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Use the compiler and versioned documentation as evidence. Do not treat a source-string check or an illustrative output as proof that a complete Swift program compiles on every platform.
